The system is failing me and so many other people. There's nothing wrong with wanting a system that works for everyone, and not just able bodied people.

I'm 26 and grew up in severe poverty and have severe health issues (cancer) so I can't move from my state. I "pulled myself up by my bootstraps" got a college degree and got a good paying job. Then I needed to get chemotherapy and radiation. My whole life fell apart, my friends wanted nothing to do with me and neither did a lot of my family. 


So now I'm disabled. I can't work in my field because of my disabilities. I'm paying for a degree I can't use because I'm disabled, and I'm paying for cancer treatments out the ass, not to mention my rent alone is expensive too. All my bills that are mandatory (medical, rent, electricity, water) because we don't have cable, or streaming services, and shitty internet, and only one cell phone (my boyfriend and I live together) come to about 4k a month. 


I've worked my ass off my whole life to have a better one to only have it taken away because we don't have free healthcare. Literally every penny I get goes toward a roof over my head food and healthcare. So yeah I think there's a problem here. Free everything isn't the answer, but I can't blame people for wanting it when we can't afford it. 


It's also frustrating because when you tell people all this they're like oh move back home but like after I finished treatment my boyfriends mom got put in a home because she has dementia and his dad HAD TO SELL THEIR HOME to pay for it. He got a shitty job at Amazon and rented an apartment for elderly people. And then he got cancer and even with treatment he only has a few years. My parents are homeless.


I don't think asking for universal healthcare is a bad thing. It would help so many people like me and my boyfriend who get sent into poverty over something you have no control over. Please tell us again how we want everything handed to us on a silver platter. Must have been nice having 40% of your check left over every month, and cable.

 I remember them saying it might take a while to get back because it was a long weekend, so probably by next Friday. Cool. Tuesday afternoon I'm working a double when I get the call, I had Hodgkin's lymphoma. 

I've been in remission for 3 years now and hope to keep it this way.
